html:
The Murrinh-Patha are an Aboriginal people of the Northern Territory, on the west coast south of the Daly River, around Port Keats. Their main town today is Wadeye, one of the largest Aboriginal communities in Australia.

A Catholic mission was founded at Port Keats in 1935, and people of several language groups settled there. Murrinh-Patha became the common language of the town, and it is still learned by children, which is rare among Aboriginal languages. Neighbours on the map include the Marrithiyel, Ngan'gimerri and Jaminjung.

The anthropologist W. E. H. Stanner studied Murrinh-Patha religion from the 1930s, and his essays on the Dreaming made this people known to scholars. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
